spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The decisive move is to compress an analytic extreme-value problem into an arithmetic optimization problem: a large GCD quadratic form supplies the coefficients that make a Dirichlet polynomial resonate strongly with zeta. The improvement is therefore controlled by how much multiplicative overlap can be packed into the GCD form, not merely by refining a zeta approximation.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Theorem 1 gives a new lower bound for extreme values of |ζ(1/2+it)| on T^β≤t≤T, compares it with earlier lower bounds, and identifies Theorem 2—a weighted lower bound for the kernel gcd(n_k,n_l)/sqrt(n_k n_l)—as the essential new input. It also recalls a general upper bound for the corresponding unweighted GCD sum and claims its leading exponent cannot be below one.
directed.conceptual_reading: The proof strategy factors into an arithmetic resource and an analytic amplifier. The GCD form measures shared multiplicative structure among the chosen integers; resonance converts that structure into a large analytic value. The parallel optimality statement makes the resource limitation visible at the same time as the gain.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge object is the positive weighted GCD matrix, viewed as a quadratic form whose near-extremizing vector becomes the coefficient profile of a resonating Dirichlet polynomial.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This unit is a result-and-method map, not the proof of either theorem. It establishes lower bounds for large zeta values, not the Riemann Hypothesis, and near-optimality of this GCD input does not imply global optimality of every possible method.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the qualitative reduction and theorem relationship. Radicals, constants, and iterated-logarithm exponents are layout-degraded, so their literal normalization requires the PDF.

That spectral relaxation is what makes a nearly extremal square-free construction usable even though the authors cannot identify an exact extremizing set.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Theorem 2 asserts that, for every fixed γ<1 and sufficiently large N, distinct integers and positive coefficients exist for which the weighted GCD quadratic form is at least the coefficient square norm times an exponential iterated-logarithm factor. directed.conceptual_reading: Weights expose the operator-norm geometry hidden by the uniform sum: the integer set supplies a kernel, while the coefficient vector selects its productive direction. Near extremality is sufficient because the later resonance argument needs the scale of the quadratic gain, not a classification of exact maximizers.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The central representation is the matrix with entries gcd(n_k,n_l)/sqrt(n_k n_l). Its positive quadratic form bridges multiplicative similarity of square-free integers to optimized resonator coefficients.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The source explicitly says that an actual extremal set is not identified. Essential optimality is therefore an asymptotic scale claim, not uniqueness or exact maximization, and the historical bounds for other σ-regimes are context rather than proofs in this unit.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the weighted-versus-uniform distinction and the near-extremizer role. Exact kernel powers, constants, and exponential normalization are extraction-sensitive.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The proof identifies its own ceiling: the resonator must obey a strict cardinality budget, and the numerator gain is routed through a GCD form already constrained by a matching upper bound. Within this architecture, further work can improve the constant only modestly unless one changes the source of gain or the representation.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The authors note that the proof repeatedly uses |M′|≤T^κ with κ≤1/2, while Soundararajan's original proof had a related restriction with κ<1. They regard such a restriction as difficult to remove. Referring to the crucial numerator estimate (25), the general GCD upper bound (1), and the comparison inequality (16), they conclude that this method can at most produce a slightly larger constant c in Theorem 1.
directed.conceptual_reading: The negative result is an architecture-specific bottleneck analysis. Cardinality limits the resonator's frequency capacity, and the GCD upper bound limits the arithmetic energy that positivity can feed into the numerator; optimizing downstream estimates cannot escape both constraints.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is the proof-budget dependency from resonator cardinality and GCD quadratic-form capacity to the numerator moment. It marks where the successful representation also forgets possible gains available to different methods.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The ceiling applies to the Soundararajan-style resonance route analyzed here, not to all methods for zeta extreme values and not to the truth of RH. The phrase slightly larger c is qualitative rather than an impossibility theorem with a universal constant.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence: the limitation is explicit prose with little extraction damage. Its scope should remain method-specific, since no argument here rules out a different resonance architecture or another analytic approach.
